title: Chest pain: history and risk
stem: Cubicle 26. Mr Yeung, 56, had 30 minutes of central chest tightness while climbing stairs this morning; it eased with rest. He is pain-free now. BP 148/88, HR 76, SpO2 98%. Take a history, then discuss the ECG, tests and disposition.
notes:
Checked against ESC 2023 ACS guidelines (0/1-hour high-sensitivity troponin algorithm), NICE CG95 (Recent-onset chest pain, updated 2016) and the HEART score (Six 2008; Backus 2013).

History: character, site, radiation, onset and trigger, duration, relief, associated symptoms (sweating, breathlessness, syncope), risk factors, and red flags for other lethal causes — aortic dissection (tearing, back, pulse deficit), PE (pleuritic, haemoptysis, DVT risk), pneumothorax, oesophageal rupture (after vomiting), pericarditis, tamponade.

ECG within 10 minutes. High-sensitivity troponin at 0 and 1 hour (or 0 and 3 h, depending on assay): rule-out, observe, or rule-in zones. HEART score (History, ECG, Age, Risk factors, Troponin): 0–3 low risk, discharge with outpatient follow-up; 4–6 intermediate; 7–10 high. Stable angina features get outpatient CT coronary angiography (NICE). Aspirin 300 mg if ACS is suspected.

Your notes' chest pain history (site, onset, radiation, exertion, associated symptoms, risk factors, drugs including cocaine/PDE5 inhibitors, differentials by system) matches.

steps.label: History
steps.hint: SOCRATES, associated symptoms, red flags for dissection/PE, risk factors, drugs.

Pain.t: Where is the pain and what is it like?
Pain.r: Central, a tight band. Went into my left arm.

Pain.t: What were you doing? What eased it? How long?
Pain.r: Climbing four flights of stairs. Eased after 30 minutes' rest.
Sweaty and short of breath with it.
Twice in the last week, shorter each time.

Red flags.t: Tearing pain into the back? Sharp pain on breathing? Coughing blood? Leg swelling?
Red flags.mark: Screens for dissection, PE and pneumothorax

Risk.t: Smoking, diabetes, BP, cholesterol, family history
Risk.r: Ex-smoker, high BP, cholesterol. Brother had bypass at 50.

Risk.mark: Drug history including PDE5 inhibitors and cocaine

steps.label: ECG and troponin
steps.hint: ECG within 10 minutes; hs-troponin 0 and 1 hour.

ECG.r: Sinus rhythm, no ST elevation or depression.

steps.label: Disposition
steps.hint: Rising troponin with typical history: NSTEMI. Treat and admit.

opts.t: Typical angina with a significant troponin rise: NSTEMI
opts.mark: Diagnoses NSTEMI from the delta troponin

opts.t: Aspirin 300 mg, anticoagulation (fondaparinux/heparin), second antiplatelet per cardiology, admit to CCU; angiography within 24 hours if high risk
HEART score is high (history 2, ECG 0, age 1, risks 2, troponin 1–2)
Pain has gone, discharge with GP follow-up
opts.r: Troponin rise with typical pain: ACS. Pain-free does not mean safe.

qs.a: History, ECG, Age, Risk factors, Troponin
wrong: Heart rate, Echo, Age, Rhythm, Temperature
Hb, ECG, Albumin, Renal function, Troponin
A single test at 12 hours after the pain

qs.a: Pulse or BP difference between arms
wrong: A pleural friction rub on auscultation
Reproducible tenderness over the costochondral joints

qs.a: PDE5 inhibitor in the last 24–48 hours
wrong: Type 2 diabetes treated with metformin and gliclazide
Age over 70 with chronic kidney disease

badge.name: Heart Scorer
badge.flavor: Typical story plus a delta troponin: it's ACS even when the pain has gone.
